chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who dyes his head with henna and then wishes to perform wudu (ablution). He said: “He wipes over the henna.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the Imam being asked for the ruling
key_terms.الْحِنَّاءِ: henna, the substance applied to the head
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)
key_terms.رَأْسَهُ: his head, the place relevant to wiping in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.فَوْقَ الْحِنَّاءِ: over the henna, indicating the manner of wiping
key_terms.يَخْضِبُ: applies dye; here, dyeing the head
key_terms.يَمْسَحُ: he wipes, referring to the masḥ required in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Can someone wipe over henna on the head during wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning wudu (ablution) when henna has been applied to the head. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that the person may perform the wiping over the henna, indicating that its presence does not prevent the validity of the masḥ in this case.
